title: Frontier Collapse
premise: A mobile-friendly top-down frontier survival game where the player chooses a role, scavenges a ruined wilderness for supplies, fights raiders or zombies, and tries to survive until the run ends.
interaction_model: Touch-first joystick movement with jump and a single context-sensitive action button for melee attacks, harvesting, biting, and build placement, plus pre-run role selection from a lobby screen.
objective: Stay alive as long as possible, gather wood and stone, fend off hostile raiders, and discover the hidden relic that unlocks the stronger Warden role.
progression: A run begins from the lobby, builds tension through time survived and resource gathering, offers optional barricade or beacon building for some roles, triggers a mid-run crew/family event, and rewards exploration with a relic unlock that changes future character choice within the session.
theme: Post-apocalyptic frontier defense with scavenging, survival, and zombie-raider pressure.
mood: Gritty, eerie, pulpy, and arcade-like, with horror-flavored title styling but bright readable HUD feedback.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy lightweight browser survival games, simple action gathering loops, mobile controls, and replayable role-based runs.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a top-down survival action game with resource gathering and light construction.
Moderate confidence that the intended fantasy mixes settlers, rangers, raiders, and a special unlockable hero in a shared frontier sandbox.
Lower confidence around long-term meta progression because the relic unlock appears session-local in code rather than persistently saved.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first full-screen browser game called "Frontier Collapse," presented as a top-down survival action sandbox on a canvas with a separate HUD overlay. The player starts in a dramatic lobby screen, enters a callsign, and picks a role such as Settler, Ranger, Raider, Brute, Scout Drone, or an unlockable Warden hero. Each role should have different health, speed, damage, and size so they feel like distinct classes. Once deployed, place the player in a large open wasteland or frontier map with simple procedural ground tiles, scattered trees, rocks, and a single rare relic hidden somewhere in the field. Use a left virtual joystick for movement, a jump button, and one context-sensitive action button that performs a short melee swing or bite in front of the character; that same action should also harvest resources when striking trees or rocks. Trees should drop wood, rocks should drop stone, and the relic should unlock the Warden role with a strong celebratory notification. Builder-oriented roles should be able to open a small build menu and spend resources to place barricades or beacon-like flags near the player. Populate the world with AI bots, especially zombie raiders that wander until they detect the player, then chase and damage them on contact. Track health, survival time, and resource counts in a sci-fi/horror HUD with chat-like status messages, floating damage text, and occasional animated feedback overlays for combat and relic moments. End the run when the player dies or survives until the timer fills, then show a death screen with the reason and total survival score in cycles. The overall tone should feel like an eerie but accessible arcade survival game: move, scavenge, strike, build a little, hunt for the relic, survive as long as possible, and redeploy for another run.
